dedupe_keys.name: humanitarian exchange language hxl tagging standard for humanitarian spreadsheets hdx support ended january 2026

description: The Humanitarian Exchange Language (HXL) is an open standard, created more than a decade ago as a simple standard for messy data, that adds HXL tags to spreadsheets, with a primary focus on combining them. The HDX team announced that from 31 January 2026 it no longer supports HXL and its tools: the hxlstandard.org website, the HXL proxy transformation tool and HDX Quick Charts are retired, and data contributors to HDX are no longer asked to add HXL tags. Coverage: global humanitarian data, much of it on HDX. Format and access: the standard remains open for organisations that want to keep using it internally, and archives of the standard site and the proxy site remain accessible; free. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (site content, except where otherwise noted). Caveats: the standard is no longer maintained by HDX, so new tools and support are unlikely; existing HXL tags on HDX datasets stay in place. Simulation uses: HXL tags in older humanitarian tables help join facility, population and incident data for emergency response and exposure studies. Related records: HOT OpenStreetMap exports on HDX (data-hotosm-country-exports-hdx) are one of the many HDX datasets that used HXL tags.
